text: The ~0.18 dB/km attenuation minimum of silica fiber near 1550 nm sits at the crossover of two wavelength-dependent loss mechanisms. Which two?
choices: Rayleigh scattering (falling as 1/lambda^4) and infrared absorption (rising above ~1700 nm)
explanation: Rayleigh scattering falls steeply as 1/lambda^4 with increasing wavelength while infrared (multiphonon) absorption rises steeply above ~1700 nm; their crossover produces the loss minimum near 1550 nm. OH absorption is a removable peak at 1383 nm, not a floor; two-photon and free-carrier absorption are nonlinear or semiconductor effects irrelevant to passive silica attenuation.
